assignments.text:
Between this soft
and yielding foundation of her life upon which she
could find no firm footing, and the rock of Catherine
Vernon who remained quite immovable and uninfluenced
by her, coming no nearer as the years went
on, yet hemming in her steps and lessening her
freedom, the conditions of existence seemed all
against the high-spirited, ambitious, active-minded
and impatient girl, with her warm affections, and
quick intelligence, and hasty disposition.
assignments.summary: Hester is trapped between her weak mother and the unyielding Catherine Vernon, her ambition and energy constrained by these two opposing forces.
assignments.best_quote: Between this soft and yielding foundation of her life upon which she could find no firm footing, and the rock of Catherine Vernon who remained quite immovable and uninfluenced by her, coming no nearer as the years went on, yet hemming in her steps and lessening her freedom, the conditions of existence seemed all against the high-spirited, ambitious, active-minded and impatient girl

assignments.text:
These might have made her close her heart against
them, and turned her into a misanthrope; but
though the effect produced was different from this,
it was not perhaps more desirable. Catherine,
though she did not become misanthropical, became
cynical, in spite of herself. She tolerated everything,
and smiled at it; she became indulgent and
contemptuous. What did it matter what they said
or felt?
assignments.summary: Catherine has become cynically indifferent to her dependents' resentment and mockery, content in her 'serene heights' of power and wealth.
assignments.best_quote: What did it matter what they said or felt?

assignments.text:
Through Catherine's mind at that moment there ran
the whole story of her later days, how she had used
herself to the pretences of all about her, how every
one around had taken from her, and snarled at her,
eaten of her bread, and drunk of her cup, and hated [Pg 186] 
her—except Edward. He alone had been her prop,
her religion of the affections.
assignments.summary: Catherine's entire adult life has been consumed by serving others who exploited her; only Edward seemed to reciprocate her devotion.
assignments.best_quote: everyone around had taken from her, and snarled at her, eaten of her bread, and drunk of her cup, and hated her—except Edward.

assignments.text:
Almost, but, alas! not quite: Catherine's prejudices
against Mrs. John's daughter, and her adverse
experiences of mankind and womankind, especially
among the Vernons, intervened, and brought her
down suddenly from that high and serious ground
upon which Hester had been capable of understanding
her. She turned away with one of those
laughs, which still brought over the girl, in her
sensitive youthfulness, a blush which was like a
blaze of angry shame.
assignments.summary: Catherine's prejudices against Mrs. John Vernon's daughter and her cynical laugh destroy the fragile moment of connection, leaving Hester humiliated and hurt.
assignments.best_quote: She turned away with one of those laughs, which still brought over the girl, in her sensitive youthfulness, a blush which was like a blaze of angry shame.

assignments.text:
Her breast swelled, her breath came short with an
impulse of impatience and longing to have such an
opportunity, to show the mettle that was in her. But how could she do it? Catherine was rich, but
Hester was poor. In this way she was diverted for
the moment from her anxiety.
assignments.summary: Hester's desire to act heroically is constrained by her poverty, which denies her the resources Catherine possessed.
assignments.best_quote: Her breast swelled, her breath came short with an impulse of impatience and longing to have such an opportunity...But how could she do it? Catherine was rich, but Hester was poor

assignments.text: "Do you?"
assignments.summary: Hester confesses her desire for achievement and renown: to be born to greatness or to earn her own significance.
assignments.best_quote: I should like to be a king's daughter or a great soldier's or a great statesman's. I should like my name to mean something. I should like people to say, when they hear it, that is——

assignments.text:
It was not
to be expected that she could grow otherwise than
contorted with the blasts. She came to the flower
and bloom of existence with a heart made to believe
and trust, yet warped to almost all around, and
finding no spot of honest standing-ground on which
to trust herself.
assignments.summary: Hester enters young adulthood with a capacity for belief but warped by her corrupting environment, unable to find solid moral ground.
assignments.best_quote: She came to the flower and bloom of existence with a heart made to believe and trust, yet warped to almost all around, and finding no spot of honest standing-ground on which to trust herself.

assignments.text:
When a
creature so young and full of life feels herself
neglected and disdained, and sees others about her
whom her keen eyes cannot help but see are inferior
to herself, promoted far above her, enjoying what is
forbidden to her, finding pleasure where she has
none—yet is bound to the spot and cannot escape, it
is natural that indignation should light fires in her
eyes, and that her breast should swell and her young
countenance glow with a visionary scorn of all who [Pg 240] 
seem to scorn her.
assignments.summary: Oliphant describes how Hester's exclusion, combined with seeing inferiors elevated above her, kindles righteous indignation and scorn.
assignments.best_quote: When a creature so young and full of life feels herself neglected and disdained, and sees others about her whom her keen eyes cannot help but see are inferior to herself, promoted far above her, enjoying what is forbidden to her, finding pleasure where she has none—yet is bound to the spot and cannot escape, it is natural that indignation should light fires in her eyes, and that her breast should swell and her young countenance glow with a visionary scorn of all who seem to scorn her

assignments.text:
She had to
consent to be bound by other people's rules, and to
put her hand to nothing that was unbecoming a
Vernon, a member of the reigning family. Small [Pg 121] 
earnings by means of sketches, or china painting,
would have been as obnoxious to Catherine Vernon's
rule as the  cours : and of what use would they have
been? It was not a little money that Hester wanted,
but work of which something good might come.
assignments.summary: Hester rejects the idea of earning small sums through sketches or painting because she seeks meaningful work, not mere money, which Catherine would anyway forbid.
assignments.best_quote: It was not a little money that Hester wanted, but work of which something good might come.

assignments.text:
Hester kept gazing through that wintry blackness,
with eyes still wide open, and her clear brows
puckered with wonder and alarm. Was it natural,
then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was
enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences,
to stand by the chief actor whatever happened,
but never to share in the initiative or have [Pg 125] 
any moral concern in the motive or the means of
what was done?
assignments.summary: Hester questions whether women's prescribed role—to sympathize and share consequences but never to understand or influence the action—is just or natural.
assignments.best_quote: Was it natural, then, a thing she could accept as just, that it was enough for her to sympathise, to share the consequences, to stand by the chief actor whatever happened, but never to share in the initiative or have any moral concern in the motive or the means of what was done?

assignments.text:
What an extraordinary shock
would it have been for his companion, who felt
herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing
the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and
exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself
was the actor, turned outside in and seen through
in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!
assignments.summary: The narrator delivers a brilliant ironic revelation: Catherine believes herself the audience observing the foolish actors of her little world, but is actually the actor being observed and judged by Edward, whom she loves.
assignments.best_quote: What an extraordinary shock would it have been for his companion, who felt herself to sit in the place of the audience, seeing the puppets play their pranks upon the stage and exhibit all their fooleries, to know that she herself was the actor, turned outside in and seen through in all her devices, to this boy whom she loved!

assignments.text:
She did not know whether he
understood what she said to him on the subject of
Harry, or if that penetrated his mind at all; but she
went home at once more miserable and more interested
than she thought she had ever been in her life. Had not she too drawn some conclusion of the same
kind from her own experiences, from the atmosphere
of the Vernonry so full of ingratitude, unkindness,
and all uncharitableness?
assignments.summary: Hester recognises that she too has absorbed the Vernonry's message that money drives human behaviour, and that the atmosphere of ingratitude and unkindness has shaped her outlook.
assignments.best_quote: Had not she too drawn some conclusion of the same kind from her own experiences, from the atmosphere of the Vernonry so full of ingratitude, unkindness, and all uncharitableness?

assignments.text:
All the same it is a pity, for the sake of young
readers, that all the girls in novels, with so very
rare exceptions—and Jane Eyre, if not pretty,
probably was less plain than she thought, and certainly
was  agaçante , which is much more effective—should
be beautiful and should have so much
admiration and conquest. The girls who read are
apt to wonder how it is that they have not the same
fortune.
assignments.summary: The narrator critiques the convention of beautiful heroines in novels, noting that such representations mislead girl readers about their own prospects.
assignments.best_quote: All the same it is a pity, for the sake of young readers, that all the girls in novels, with so very rare exceptions—and Jane Eyre, if not pretty, probably was less plain than she thought, and certainly was agaçante, which is much more effective—should be beautiful and should have so much admiration and conquest. The girls who read are apt to wonder how it is that they have not the same fortune.

assignments.text:
Disagreeable things were
indeed said about "genteel almshouses," and "poor
relations," when it first became a question in
Redborough about calling on the new residents. But, as it turned out, they were all persons of pretensions,
expecting to be called upon by the county,
and contemptuous of the townspeople.
assignments.summary: Redborough society questioned whether to call on the Vernonry residents, gossiping about 'genteel almshouses' and 'poor relations,' but the residents proved themselves persons of pretension.
assignments.best_quote: Disagreeable things were indeed said about 'genteel almshouses,' and 'poor relations,' when it first became a question in Redborough about calling on the new residents.

assignments.text:
And I
must be on my ps and qs with this little girl. There
is a great deal of fun to be got out of her; but we
must keep it strictly to ourselves."
assignments.summary: Catherine tells Edward that Hester is amusing material for entertainment, but they must keep their mockery private.
assignments.best_quote: There is a great deal of fun to be got out of her; but we must keep it strictly to ourselves.

assignments.text:
Catherine had to follow a mazy, vague, and
wandering clue thus, through acres of indifferent
matter, and to piece together broken scraps of
information which were never intended to affect her
at all.
assignments.summary: Catherine must work through Emma's rambling monologues to extract the small fragments of relevant information.
assignments.best_quote: Catherine had to follow a mazy, vague, and wandering clue thus, through acres of indifferent matter, and to piece together broken scraps of information

assignments.text:
"They said they would
come and fetch you to spend a day with them,
didn't they? Then why don't they come, Hester?—why
don't they come?" the poor lady said. Hester's anger and wretchedness and nervous irritation
were such that she could almost have struck
her mother. Was it right, in addition to her own
disappointment, that she should have this question
thrust upon her, and that all the pangs of
her first disenchantment should be discussed by contemptuous
spectators?
assignments.summary: Mrs. John's repeated questioning about Ellen's absence drives Hester nearly to violence, adding insult to injury.
assignments.best_quote: 'They said they would come and fetch you to spend a day with them, didn't they? Then why don't they come, Hester?—why don't they come?' the poor lady said. Hester's anger and wretchedness and nervous irritation were such that she could almost have struck her mother.

assignments.text:
Hester made no reply to this praise. Her heart
was beating more quickly than usual. What she
had said was quite true: but all the time, though
he had been ready to laugh, and though she had
been ready to laugh, she was aware that there was
something more. The tone of banter had not been
all. The sense of something humorous, under those
high-flown phrases, had not exhausted them.
assignments.summary: The narrator reveals that Hester's heart beats faster as she consciously recognizes the truth beneath Roland's banter—that genuine feeling underlies his playfulness.
assignments.best_quote: Her heart was beating more quickly than usual. What she had said was quite true: but all the time, though he had been ready to laugh, and though she had been ready to laugh, she was aware that there was something more. The tone of banter had not been all. The sense of something humorous, under those high-flown phrases, had not exhausted them.

assignments.text:
In this way the spring went on. It had appeared
to Edward himself as certain that some great  coup 
must have settled his fate long before. It was his
inexperience, perhaps, and the excitement of his
determination to act for himself, which had made
everything appear so imminent; but after all it did
not turn out so. The course of events went on in
that leisurely current which is far more deadly in its
sweep than any sudden cataract.
assignments.summary: Edward's financial ventures proceed gradually and indecisively, with neither clear gain nor catastrophic loss, but slow accumulation of danger.
assignments.best_quote: The course of events went on in that leisurely current which is far more deadly in its sweep than any sudden cataract.

assignments.text:
Edward, for his part, returned to his room, and
shut himself in with feelings much less victorious
than those he made apparent. The excitement of
the great decision had a little failed and gone off. He was in the chill reactionary stage, wondering
what might befall, feeling the tugs of old prejudice,
of all the traditions of honour in which he had been
brought up, dragging at his heart.
assignments.summary: Edward returns to his room in a state of emotional collapse, the excitement of his decision wearing off, replaced by anxiety and the torment of his moral training.
assignments.best_quote: He was in the chill reactionary stage, wondering what might befall, feeling the tugs of old prejudice, of all the traditions of honour in which he had been brought up, dragging at his heart

assignments.text:
Had there been only the risks of the crisis, the
meeting of alarmed and anxious creditors, the chance
even of criminal prosecution, he might have faced it;
but to return again to that old routine, to take up
his former life, was impossible. He flew along like
the wind. There was still an hour or more before
the train would start. Would the women gather
themselves together, he wondered, soon enough to
send after him, to prevent his journey?
assignments.summary: Edward reflects that he might have faced financial ruin and prosecution, but cannot bear to return to his ordinary former life; he resolves to walk to the train junction.
assignments.best_quote: Had there been only the risks of the crisis, the meeting of alarmed and anxious creditors, the chance even of criminal prosecution, he might have faced it; but to return again to that old routine, to take up his former life, was impossible.

assignments.text:
"We must not fight," he said, "my only love. I
am going away, and I can't quarrel with you, my
only love! And I am your only love. There has
never been anybody between us. I will come back
in two or three days; but Hester, another time, if it
should be for good, would you come?—you would
come?—with me?"
assignments.summary: Edward announces he must leave briefly but asks if Hester would come away with him permanently if needed, seeking her commitment to flight.
assignments.best_quote: if it should be for good, would you come?—you would come?—with me?

assignments.text:
What had
the crisis been through which he had passed? What
was the new departure, the burning of the ships? There must be some serious meaning in words so
serious as these. And then that wild suggestion
that she should fly with him, whether they gained
or lost, "away from all this; you don't love it any
more than I do"—what did that mean? Alarm was
in her mind along with the excitement of a secret
half-revealed.
assignments.summary: Hester questions what grave crisis Edward has passed through and what 'burning ships' signifies; his proposal of elopement 'win or lose' alarms her with its implications of great risk.
assignments.best_quote: What had the crisis been through which he had passed? What was the new departure, the burning of the ships? There must be some serious meaning in words so serious as these. And then that wild suggestion that she should fly with him, whether they gained or lost... what did that mean?

assignments.text:
The most wonderful complication of all, the companionship
in which he had left England, was not
told to her then. It threw to all the others a
horrible mockery upon the whole story.
assignments.summary: The narrator hints at a remarkable discovery: Edward's companion in his departure from England, a detail kept from Catherine initially.
assignments.best_quote: The most wonderful complication of all, the companionship in which he had left England, was not told to her then.

assignments.text:
There were not even any heavings
and groanings, like those that warn the surrounding
country before a volcano bursts forth. Nevertheless,
this girl, who had been so long a spectator, [Pg 22] 
pushed aside from the action about her, but with
the keen sight of injured pride and wounded feeling,
seeing the secret thread of meaning that ran
through everything, felt premonitions, she could not
tell how, in the heated air, and through the
domestic calm.
assignments.summary: The narrator eloquently describes Hester's sensitive perception of imminent crisis; despite outward calm, she senses approaching danger like a volcano about to erupt, perceiving hidden meaning beneath surface tranquility.
assignments.best_quote: All was still, and everything going on in its calm habitual way. There were not even any heavings and groanings, like those that warn the surrounding country before a volcano bursts forth. Nevertheless, this girl, who had been so long a spectator, pushed aside from the action about her, but with the keen sight of injured pride and wounded feeling, seeing the secret thread of meaning that ran through everything, felt premonitions, she could not tell how, in the heated air, and through the domestic calm.

assignments.text:
She was aware of the very tone in which
these speeches would be made, as well as if she had
heard them, and it gave her a great sense of enjoyment
to reflect that they were all sitting in rooms
well warmed and carefully kept, and full of benevolent
prevision of all their wants, while they thus
permitted themselves to sneer and snarl at the
bestower.
assignments.summary: Catherine takes pleasure in knowing that her dependents sneer at her while enjoying the comforts she provides.
assignments.best_quote: she gave her a great sense of enjoyment to reflect that they were all sitting in rooms well warmed and carefully kept, and full of benevolent prevision of all their wants, while they thus permitted themselves to sneer and snarl at the bestower

assignments.text:
The rage with which she would
contemplate herself when she yielded to the first
temptation and launched at Cousin Catherine in a
moment of passion one of those arrows which were
manufactured in the Vernonry, the deep disgust
which would fill her when she felt herself, like
Catherine, contemplating the world from a pinnacle
of irony, chill but smiling, swept her young spirit
like tempests. To grow at all in the midst of such
gales and whirlwinds was something.
assignments.summary: Hester's self-reproach for moments of cruelty to Catherine and adoption of Catherine's cynicism sweeps over her like violent storms, causing deep psychological turmoil.
assignments.best_quote: The rage with which she would contemplate herself when she yielded to the first temptation and launched at Cousin Catherine in a moment of passion one of those arrows which were manufactured in the Vernonry, the deep disgust which would fill her when she felt herself, like Catherine, contemplating the world from a pinnacle of irony, chill but smiling, swept her young spirit like tempests.

assignments.text:
It was scarcely
one o'clock, but in summer there is little night, and
already the air had begun to whiten with some premonition
of day. She held up her face to the sky—an
old face, with so many lines in it, suddenly [Pg 198] 
smitten as with a death-blow. Her eyes, under the
curve of pain, which makes the eyelids quiver, looked
up to the pale skies with what is the last appeal of
humanity.
assignments.summary: As dawn breaks, Catherine lifts her aged, grief-stricken face to the paling sky in a gesture of ultimate human appeal and anguish.
assignments.best_quote: Her eyes, under the curve of pain, which makes the eyelids quiver, looked up to the pale skies with what is the last appeal of humanity.

assignments.text:
Flying fast
across the country somewhere, directing his way, no
doubt, to some port where he could get out of England. For what, oh Heaven, for what? Was there
any sacrifice she would not have made for him? He
might have had his Hester, his own house like the
others, if that was what he wanted. There was
nothing, nothing she would have grudged him! She
would have asked no gratitude, made no conditions.
assignments.summary: Catherine's anguished fantasy: she would have gladly given Edward freedom, allowed him Hester, and asked nothing in return—but he fled without asking.
assignments.best_quote: He might have had his Hester, his own house like the others, if that was what he wanted. There was nothing, nothing she would have grudged him! She would have asked no gratitude, made no conditions.

assignments.text:
And the silence resumed its sway. She laid
herself back as before—her pale head against the
dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time
afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily,
then there was no sound at all. The fire burned
cheerfully, the lamp shed its steady glow upon
Hester's book, to which after this talk she did not,
as may be supposed, pay very much attention.
assignments.summary: Catherine lays back with her pale head against dark curtains and becomes still. Hours pass as Hester reads, then a supernatural chill sweeps through the warm room as Hester realises Catherine's hands have grown cold.
assignments.best_quote: her pale head against the dark curtains stood out like ivory. Some time afterwards she sighed two or three times heavily, then there was no sound at all... A chill crept into the room like nothing Hester had ever felt before, though all was still, serenely warm and bright to outward appearance.

assignments.text:
The air did not do Hester good: the shade of the
holly-tree lying motionless upon the road, the half
open gate at which Catherine had appeared in the darkness,
the strange intelligence that seemed to be in
every bush, as if these inanimate things knew and
remembered what had been done and said in secret,
seemed to bring conviction, and force back upon her
all the scenes she had gone through of which her
innocent mother knew nothing.
assignments.summary: As Hester walks home with her mother, every detail of the landscape—the holly tree, the gate, even the bushes—seems to know and recall the secret trauma of the previous night.
assignments.best_quote: the shade of the holly-tree lying motionless upon the road, the half open gate at which Catherine had appeared in the darkness, the strange intelligence that seemed to be in every bush
